<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via directSignIn (literal, a string literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via IP_NOT_ALLOWED (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_NETWORK_REFUSED))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via IP_NOT_ALLOWED (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_NETWORK_REFUSED))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via IP_NOT_ALLOWED (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_NETWORK_REFUSED), callbackURL (literal, a string literal in directSignInNetworkRefusal))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via IP_NOT_ALLOWED (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_NETWORK_REFUSED), callbackURL (literal, a string literal in directSignInNetworkRefusal), directSignIn (literal, a string literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER), /api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct (route, a path literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in directSignInNetworkRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via IP_NOT_ALLOWED (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_NETWORK_REFUSED))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ec7b93c28ddbd80483fcb4e878ca2bea6a316db` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a7c464d4054d2437e7f2b4005d913e9d3000236a` — the merge of head `e25b4e31a6be0e0cc5aca0fcae4a0779a678dd84` into base `6ec7b93c28ddbd80483fcb4e878ca2bea6a316db`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a7c464d4054d2437e7f2b4005d913e9d3000236a && git checkout a7c464d4054d2437e7f2b4005d913e9d3000236a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ec7b93c28ddbd80483fcb4e878ca2bea6a316db e25b4e31a6be0e0cc5aca0fcae4a0779a678dd84 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ec7b93c28ddbd80483fcb4e878ca2bea6a316db && git merge --no-ff e25b4e31a6be0e0cc5aca0fcae4a0779a678dd84

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ec7b93c28ddbd80483fcb4e878ca2bea6a316db
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ec7b93c28ddbd80483fcb4e878ca2bea6a316db` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — FAIL

Head-sha: `10180db4984626bb606c06c25ad39a857a60ca96`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T10:53Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `b76df9a6` (matches the PR files list: 24 files, +546/−72)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv (area S1 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM, with one isolated read-only sub-agent for the diff, findings re-checked here

**What holds**

- Premise: the three items left open on #33358 after #33623 (rulings 6888442664, 6889573269) are real on main. The settings save reads only `config.emailPassword`; the allow-list middleware answers every blocked request with the 403 JSON; the sign-out note is a bare time honoured on any load in the window. The diff delivers those and nothing beyond.
- The access boundary (area's item 2), confirmed in code. The 302 target is `getConsoleUrl('/login')`, built from the configured canonical origin, never Host or Referer. The carried `?redirect=` passes `keptReturnPath` on both layers, and a foreign one is dropped (pinned). The middleware returns before `next()`, so the door handler never runs: no credential read, no session, no cookie (pinned). The refusal is still explained and audited first. Only `GET` on the exact door path while the door is mounted gets the 302. POST, HEAD, other auth paths, a trailing slash, and every request while direct sign-in is off still answer `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, with status and code asserted. No identifier is read, so account existence is not exposed. In the ledger only the note text moved.
- The floor logic (every branch walked). Under `hidden`, or with direct sign-in off, every answer is identical to main. Under `off`, no save ends with no way in, and a save that keeps another way in is not refused. `localSignIn` is not a settings key, so one save cannot flip it.
- The i18n key `auth.login.errors.networkNotAllowed` is in all 11 packs with real translations, and consumed by `ssoCallbackRefusal.ts`. `googleLocalOff` is in all 11 floor locales. Hot file: this PR's `auth-plugin.ts` hunks (imports; the allow-list middleware) do not overlap #33268's hunk (`set-initial-password`). Positional shift only.

**Must-fix**

1. **The Clause-② arm is wrong: this PR narrows.** Under `localSignIn: 'off'`, a settings save that turns Google off (or clears an unbacked Google credential) while email and password is on was accepted on main. It now answers `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` (`googleLocalOff`). That removes an accepted request, the same kind of change #33623 made to the provider delete and declared as `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with `!`, BREAKING, the ADR-0087 disposition and the dogfood battery. Re-declare this PR the same way, in the PR body and the changeset: narrowed (the save refusal above, and the blocked door `GET` now answering `302` to `/login?error=IP_NOT_ALLOWED` where it answered `403` JSON); widened (the new i18n key, the floor copy key, the module exports). Then add the `Skills-docs:` line the narrowing arm requires, `!` in the title, the BREAKING note, the ADR-0087 disposition and a dogfood battery run at the new head.
   The declared narrowing moves this PR's review face to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (scope: the whole diff outside the prose faces). The full contract-review record will be written at the corrected head at that tier, not at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

**Should-fix (fold into the same round)**

2. The "`email_password_enabled` is never refused under `off`" pins (`sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` ~485 and ~943) keep Google in force, so they stay green with that guard deleted. Add the case where nothing else is in force, and ablate the guard.
3. These boundary pins have no ablation evidence: the method/path check in `isDirectSignInDoorNavigation` (POST, other paths and a trailing slash still answer 403), and the `directSignInDoorMounted` gate (direct sign-in off still answers 403). Ablate each and report the red.
4. Docs: neither `sso.mdx` nor the `allowed_ip_ranges` section of `authentication.mdx` says that a blocked browser `GET` of the door now lands on `/login?error=IP_NOT_ALLOWED`. Add one sentence.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

5. The floor refusal pins assert the code but not the 400. This follows the file's existing pattern, and envelope conformance covers the mapping.
6. Any `GET` of the door path gets the 302, whatever its `Accept` header. This is harmless because the door was already 302-only for allowed clients.

**Gates:** not judged. At review time 25 check-runs were in progress, 32 success, 9 skipped, none red.

Next: a new head with items 1–4. I review the delta, and the contract-review record is written at that head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c6c999ce249c9cc9604082fddc10366db8a3528`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/direct-sign-in.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/direct-sign-in.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts`, `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/LoginPage.direct-sign-in.test.tsx`, `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/ssoCallbackRefusal.ts`, `ui/packages/auth/src/__tests__/signOutRoundTrip-33183.test.tsx`, `ui/packages/auth/src/createAuthClient.ts`, `ui/packages/auth/src/signOutRoundTrip.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/ar.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/de.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/es.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/fr.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/ja.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/ko.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/pt-BR.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/ru.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/zh-Hans.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/zh-Hant.ts` + read, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts`, `ui/packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx`, `ui/packages/auth/src/AuthProvider.tsx`, `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx`, `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/directSignIn.ts`, `ui/apps/console/src/App.tsx`, `docs/adr/0069-enterprise-authentication-hardening.md`, `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`

Read: card #33358 with its ten comments, PR #33781's body, file list and five comments, and the net diff against the merge's main parent `b76df9a6` (24 files, +585/−72; the file list equals the API's). The cited code and the published spec were read on `origin/main`. Nothing was built or run.

Check-runs on this head: 72, of which 61 success and 11 skipped, none failed, none still running when this was written (12:02Z). A second `Check Changeset` run was in progress at my first read (started 11:56Z) and completed success at 11:58Z.

### ① Derived judgments

No must-fix.

Each answer the diff moves, against `main`:

- **Settings save under `off`, Google last: 200 → 400. Declared, right.** `signInMethodFloorPredicate` (`sign-in-method-floor.ts:703-728`) now sets `emailPasswordAfter` false whenever `pageOffersLocalSignIn` is false, and counts phone only as the page offers it. I walked every return under `off`: a Google change is refused only when Google was in force, no other social or OIDC provider with credentials, no identity provider row and no host handoff stands, and Google is gone after the save. Under `hidden`, or with direct sign-in off, `localOffered` is true and every line reads as on `main`.
- **Blocked `GET` of the door: 403 JSON → 302. Declared, right.** See ④.
- **Settings save under `off`, the email and password key: 400 → 200. Not declared.** This is S1 below.
- **Additive surface, declared, right:** the module exports `DIRECT_SIGN_IN_NETWORK_REFUSED`, `isDirectSignInDoorNavigation`, `directSignInNetworkRefusal` (not on the package entry); `googleLocalOff`, a required field of `SignInFloorCopy`, present in all 11 locales; `auth.login.errors.networkNotAllowed` in all 11 packs. No new error code: `IP_NOT_ALLOWED` is already in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:660`.
- **`markSignOutRoundTrip(returnPath, now)`: a changed signature, right.** `signOutRoundTrip.ts` is not exported from the `@object-ui/auth` entry, and its one caller is in the diff.
- **The sign-out note: right.** The note's path is `resolveSpaRoute('/login')`, the same value the sign-out sends as `callbackURL`, which the server turns into the provider's return address (`sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts:371-375`). The Console's router basename comes from the same `base` element (`App.tsx:133`), so the path loaded on return is the path recorded. `AuthProvider` still clears the note on every mount, so a deep link drops it unread. A note in the old bare-number shape parses to a number, has no `path`, and reads as no note.

**S1 (should-fix) — one moved answer is undeclared, and the changeset calls it unchanged**

- On `main`, under `off`, saving `email_password_enabled: false` with nothing else in force (no Google, no other provider, no identity provider row, no handoff, no phone) is refused `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` with the `emailPassword` copy. The predicate on `main` reaches its last line for that key.
- At this head the new guard at `sign-in-method-floor.ts:711` returns before any check, so the same save answers 200. The pin `under the local sign-in path off, the email and password key is never refused, even with no other way in configured` asserts exactly that.
- A second, smaller move: the batch that turns email and password and the last Google off together under `off` is still refused, but now at the Google key only, where `main` reported both keys.
- The changeset's `Unchanged:` paragraph (line 18) lists "the `email_password_enabled` switch, which is never refused under `off`". That is true of the head and false as a statement about what changed. The `Widened:` list on the `Clause-②:` line, in the changeset and the PR body, does not name it.
- The behaviour itself is defensible, and I do not ask for it to change. In that state the page already offers nothing, the boot report already says so at error, and without the guard every save that carries the key would be refused there, including one that turns it on. But the save does turn off a server door that still answers (`POST /sign-in/email` is unchanged by `off`, as the spec says), so recovery then needs `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true` as well as the local path. An operator should read that in the release note.
- Fix, on the prose faces only: name this move under `Widened:` in the changeset and the PR body, take the sentence out of `Unchanged:`, and say in "What to do" that recovery after it needs both settings. No source line needs to move.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right arm, and the title carries `!`. Two answers narrow, as declared.
- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@object-ui/console`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/auth` matches what the diff publishes and follows #33623. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- The changeset has one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. That is right: no stored key, accepted value or metadata type moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.
- The BREAKING paragraph names both narrowed answers, who is affected and what to do. The one gap in the changeset's account is S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report's `open_questions` is empty. Its two out-of-scope notes need no ruling: a `HEAD` to the door from a blocked client still answers 403 (true, `isDirectSignInDoorNavigation` matches `GET` only), and a note written by the previous release reads as no note (true, see ①).
- Claim amendment 6893265267 asked for the full arm text, a `Skills-docs:` line, `!`, BREAKING, the ADR-0087 disposition and a dogfood battery at the head. All are present, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on this head.
- The diff touches no `packages/spec` file, no generated file and no release-owned page. `auth-plugin.ts` is touched in the import block and the allow-list middleware only.
- All four items the card still held after #33623 (the settings-save half of item 1, item 2, item 5 and nit N6) are in this diff, so `Fixes #33358` is right.

### ④ Design judgment

**The settings save makes the floor's own refusal real. It takes no declared capability away.**
- The spec on `main` declares `localSignIn: 'off'` as "the sign-in form offers no local way in" (`auth-endpoints.zod.ts:295`). The page implements it: `LoginForm.tsx:349-354` hides email and password and both phone ways under `off`. The floor's declared job is to keep a way in on that page, and since #33623 the provider delete and the boot report already judge by `pageOffersLocalSignIn`. This diff brings the third door to the same predicate, as release note 6889573269 asked.
- The capability an administrator loses is saving the page into "No sign-in method is available". Nothing the spec declares is narrowed at a consumer.
- Tried to break it. `localSignIn` is not a settings key, so one save cannot flip it under the predicate. A batch that turns email and password on beside Google off is still refused, because `localOffered` gates the email leg. An identity provider store that cannot be read counts as no row, so the save refuses, as on `main`. The copy's last remedy (local path back to `hidden` with email and password on) is true: the environment variable wins over the option in `resolveDirectSignIn`.

**The blocked door keeps the allow-list's refusal whole and changes only its shape for one navigation.**
- ADR-0069 D5 decides "a gate ahead of the better-auth handler, refusing with `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`". The middleware still explains and audits first, and returns without calling `next()`, so the door never runs: no provider read, no vendor state, no cookie (pinned with `getSetCookie()` empty). The landing carries the same code.
- The exception is as narrow as it can be: `GET`, the exact mounted path, and only while `directSignInDoorMounted` is true. The flag is read per request, so a door that was never mounted keeps the 403. `POST`, a trailing slash, every other auth path and direct sign-in off are pinned at 403 with the code.
- No open redirect. The origin comes from `getConsoleUrl`, never from the request. `callbackURL` must appear once and pass `keptReturnPath`, and the `redirect` inside it passes the same rule again in `carriedRedirect`; the query is built with `URLSearchParams`. A foreign value lands on the bare page (pinned).
- No loop. A URL with `error` is a `hold` in `decideDirectSignIn`, so the page does not navigate again; the retry button starts only on a click, which is useful after the person joins the VPN. `/config` stays exempt, so the page can draw.
- Nothing new is disclosed: a blocked client could already learn that direct sign-in is on from the exempt `/config`.

**Nits (none blocks).**
- N1. The spec says of `localSignIn` "It changes no server door: password sign-in answers the same either way" (`auth-endpoints.zod.ts:295-299`, `public-auth-features.ts:399-405`). The sign-in doors are indeed unchanged, but two other doors now answer by it: the provider delete since #33623 and the settings save here. The sentence should say "no sign-in door". It is a `packages/spec` edit, so it belongs on a follow-up card, not in this PR.
- N2. `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx:652` still says a refused request answers `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` with no mention of the door's landing. `sso.mdx` now carries the sentence and links there. One clause in the field row would close it; the page is outside the claim's surface, so a follow-up.
- N3. `googleLocalOff` offers "set up another sign-in method before or in this save". Under `off` the auth settings form holds no other method that counts (email and password does not, and Google is the one being removed), so "or in this save" tells the reader nothing there. The other remedies in the sentence are true.
- N4. `ssoCallbackRefusal.ts` says the network sentence names "the administrator, not a retry", while the page still draws the retry button under it. Both are fine; the comment could say the button stays.

S1 is open on this head. It earns a delta review of its fix before this PR lands.

Head-sha: `7c6c999ce249c9cc9604082fddc10366db8a3528`

Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

**Items of 6893256448, all closed at this head**
1. Clause-② is re-declared `yes (narrowing)` in the #33623 form, with `!` in the title, BREAKING, the `adr-0087: not-required` marker, `Skills-docs: none` and the dogfood battery (`Dogfood Regression Gate` green on this head). Closed.
2. A nothing-else-in-force pin was added for the email key under `off`, with a control under `hidden`. The ablation in the area's report turns exactly those pins red. Closed.
3. A trailing-slash case was added. The method check, the path equality and `directSignInDoorMounted` are each ablated red. Closed.
4. `sso.mdx` gained the blocked-door 302 sentence. Checked against `direct-sign-in.ts` and `auth-plugin.ts` at this head: true. ("a browser `GET`" is any `GET`, accepted as nit 6 of the first round.) Closed.

**Contract review (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, narrowing face):** record 6894038792 on this head, **VERDICT: PASS**, rendered by an isolated at-tier sub-agent from the `--brief-template` brief (below) and adopted by this seat. Before adopting it I checked three things: the `Scope:` line covers every path outside the prose faces (the narrowing floor), the independence pair is present, and the record judges the tree rather than the PR body. It records no must-fix and one should-fix:

**Open (should-fix, prose faces only, no source line moves)**
